answer.location_description: Bottom-left corner of the image, roughly rows 18-22 and columns 0-3, on the image border far from the centred nodule.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units carry it. The 'benign' units (positive bias: 3, 5, 14, 15, 19, 21, 23, 24, 26, 28) have their most negative peripheral weights in the bottom-left corner block, so a bright patch there switches them off. These units feed the output negatively through layer-2 units u1, u2, u7, u8 and u15; for example, unit 26 contributes a strongly negative net amount to the logit. The 'malignant' units (negative bias: 11, 16, 20, 27, 30, 0) have positive weights in the same corner. They feed u1, u2, u8 and u15, which have large positive output weights (80, 99, 60, 64). A bright bottom-left patch therefore both removes benign evidence and adds malignant evidence, raising the logit.
answer.evidence: In the benign units, the 3x3 corner averages around rows 19-21, cols 0-2 are about -40 (unit 3: -52 -23 -34 / -54 -64 -32), -34 (unit 5), -38 (unit 15), -29 (unit 28), -27 (unit 26) and -23 (unit 21). For the same units the top-right corner averages about -10 to -20, and the top-left and bottom-right corners are near 0 or positive. The malignant-type units are consistently positive there: unit 30 bottom-left about +32 (39 22 51 / 22 34 41), unit 27 about +21, unit 11 row 19 reads 43 63 67. These units feed the logit positively: unit 30 and unit 27 have net contributions of roughly +20k in integer units through u1, u2, u9 and u15. The corner is not part of the nodule, which is centred and spans about 12 pixels. The asymmetry across corners is consistent and goes beyond a symmetric surround detector. A weaker but similar asymmetry exists at the top-right edge, so the evidence is moderate rather than conclusive.
answer.main_feature: The benign-leaning units detect a compact, well-circumscribed central blob with a dark lung ring around it. The malignant-leaning units respond to bright tissue extending into the surrounding annulus and periphery, consistent with irregular, spiculated or attached nodules.
